understanding: FileSnapshotSink.Cancel shares an in-memory closed flag with Close. A first cancellation sets that flag before finalization and removes the temporary directory only if finalization succeeds. Subsequent cancellation returns nil without checking or retrying cleanup, including after a failed Close or Cancel. Temporary directories are excluded from snapshot listing. These observations distinguish terminal-call admission, cleanup completion, and snapshot publication.

behaviors.protocol_context: Built-in file snapshot sink with closed == false
behaviors.trigger: Cancel invoked before a terminal call has set closed
legal_preconditions: A successfully created sink supplies initialized buffered writer, state file and checksum state.
Description of sequential terminal calls does not assume concurrent calls are supported.
implementation_guards: Return immediately if closed is already true.
reads: closed, buffered, stateFile, noSync, stateHash and dir
writes: On successful finalization, set meta.Size and meta.CRC.
durable_effects: Finalization flushes buffered state and, unless noSync, syncs the state file.
After successful finalization, invoke os.RemoveAll on the temporary directory.
No parent-directory synchronization follows cancellation removal.
external_effects: Return the finalization error immediately, or return the result of os.RemoveAll.
important_branches: Flush or Sync failure returns before the state-file Close and before directory removal.
Stat is attempted before state-file Close; its error is returned after a successful Close.
State-file Close failure returns before directory removal.
Successful finalization followed by failed removal leaves closed true and returns the removal error.
existing_protections: Cancellation does not rename the temporary directory into the published snapshot namespace.
getSnapshots excludes directories whose names end in .tmp, including temporary artifacts left by failed cleanup.
The closed guard suppresses repeated terminal work.
unknowns: Actual caller handling of cancellation errors and cleanup of abandoned temporary directories are outside this expansion.
Concurrent terminal-call and Write behavior is not established by the supplied interface contract.
Crash persistence of successful removal is not established.

behaviors.protocol_context: The same sink object after Close or Cancel has set closed
legal_preconditions: A prior terminal-call entry set the shared flag; that call need not have succeeded.
external_effects: Return nil without finalization, removal, publication-state inspection or retry.
important_branches: The same return applies after successful cancellation, failed cancellation, successful closure and failed closure.
existing_protections: Repeated cancellation does not repeat terminal filesystem operations.
unknowns: A nil return on this branch does not reveal whether artifacts remain, handles were closed, or a snapshot was published.

behaviors.protocol_context: Built-in file snapshot sink sharing terminal state with Cancel
legal_preconditions: A successfully created sink supplies initialized resources.
implementation_guards: If closed is already true, return nil without further work.
reads: closed, buffered, stateFile, stateHash, noSync, dir, parentDir, meta and store
writes: Set closed = true before finalization on the first terminal call.
Successful finalization updates meta.Size and meta.CRC.
Write final metadata before renaming the directory.
durable_effects: Finalize state, write metadata and rename the temporary directory to a path without .tmp.
When noSync is false and the platform is not Windows, open and sync the parent directory.
Invoke ReapSnapshots after publication and applicable parent synchronization.
external_effects: Return errors from finalization, cleanup, metadata writing, rename, parent-directory operations or reaping.
Return nil when all reached operations succeed or the closed guard takes effect.
important_branches: Unlike Cancel, a finalization failure triggers an attempt to remove the temporary directory; a removal error replaces the returned finalization error.
Metadata or rename failure returns with closed still true.
Parent-directory or reaping failure occurs after successful rename, so an error return does not imply absence from the published namespace.
No error branch resets closed; subsequent Cancel performs no cleanup.
existing_protections: Temporary names are excluded from listing.
State and metadata synchronization are enabled unless noSync is set.
Parent-directory synchronization is attempted on the enabled non-Windows path.
Finalization failure has an explicit cleanup attempt.
unknowns: This supporting description does not establish snapshot recoverability or filesystem crash guarantees.
Caller interpretation of a post-publication Close error remains unread.

facts.meaning: A terminal call on this sink object has set closed to true. This establishes suppression of subsequent sequential Close and Cancel work, not successful finalization, cleanup or publication.

identity.sink: The specific FileSnapshotSink object; the flag is not keyed solely by snapshot ID or directory.

facts.validity_context: Established at the closed assignment in the first Close or Cancel call, before fallible I/O. Applies to subsequent sequential calls on that object.
facts.recovery: No persistent reconstruction of this flag is shown; retained directories do not encode terminal-call success.
unknowns: No concurrent-call synchronization contract is established.
The flag alone cannot distinguish either terminal method's successful and failed outcomes.

facts.meaning: On the first cancellation path, finalization and os.RemoveAll(s.dir) both returned successfully. This is distinct from a nil return through the already-closed branch.

identity.sink: The FileSnapshotSink object executing its first Cancel path
identity.artifact_path: s.dir, initialized by Create to the store path plus snapshot name and .tmp

facts.validity_context: Established only at successful completion of removal after successful finalization. It records that operation's outcome, not permanent absence under subsequent filesystem activity.
representation: Control flow reaches os.RemoveAll(s.dir) and it returns nil.
facts.durability: Filesystem removal completed according to the API return; cancellation does not sync the parent directory.
facts.recovery: Crash recovery of removed or residual artifacts is not established. Listing independently skips .tmp directories.
unknowns: No actual consumer of this branch-specific completion assertion has been inspected.
Directory-name uniqueness, concurrent path reuse and persistence across crash are not established.

surfaces.reason: The supplied implementation resolves first-call cleanup, finalization failure, removal failure and already-closed cancellation. The directly connected Close path explains how the shared flag can suppress cancellation after failure or publication. Creation and listing establish the temporary-path context. Mapping records this behavior without asserting cleanup or recovery correctness.

delta.rationale: Expand only the cancellation frontier and its directly connected terminal-state lifecycle. The interface describes Cancel as the unsuccessful-end path but supplies no detailed cleanup or retry guarantee. Implementation observations therefore support separate facts for terminal-call latching and successful removal, while preserving listing exclusion, synchronization variants, Close cleanup and post-rename error paths as relevant mechanisms. No normative obligation or defect is inferred.

limitations: Caller error handling, actual adapter selection and restart cleanup were not inspected.
No execution, crash experiment or concurrency check was performed.
The mapped surface is descriptive understanding, not evidence of overall correctness.
